title: Capture sessions
description: Output of `python3 -m capture sessions`. Times are integer nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, durations are milliseconds, and the client of a session is the side that opened it, or the side that the extractor guessed (see roles). SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only

file.description: Base name of the capture file.

frames.description: Frames read, after the interface filter.

packets.description: Frames decoded to TCP segments or UDP datagrams.

skipped_frames.description: Frames that were not decoded, counted by reason: not_ip, fragment, truncated_header, bad_header, unsupported_l4, unsupported_link_type.

id.description: Counts interfaces over the whole file, across pcapng sections.

tsresol.description: Timestamp resolution of the interface, such as 1e-6 or 2^-10.

sessions.description: Ordered by start time. Ids start at 1 and follow that order.

scrub.description: Written by `capture scrub` (CAP-03), and only by it. The scenario generator sets `scrubbed: true` in a manifest only for an intact record. It never holds a value that was removed.

capture_sha256.description: Digest of the capture file, when the sessions document recorded it.

input_sha256.description: Digest of the unscrubbed sessions file.

learned.description: How many distinct addresses, email addresses, host names and other values were replaced.

opaque_bytes.description: Bytes of binary payload, which the scrubber only sweeps for learned values.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the document without this field, as sorted compact JSON. It catches an edit after scrubbing; it does not stop someone who recomputes it.

client_known.description: True when a SYN or SYN ACK fixed the roles.

basis.description: syn: the client sent the first SYN. synack: the server answered. port: exactly one port is below 1024 and that side is the server. first_packet: the sender of the first packet seen. A UDP flow that continues after an idle split keeps the roles of the flow.

interfaces.description: Ids of the capture interfaces that saw packets of this session.

duration_ms.description: From the first to the last packet.

data_start_ns.description: First packet with payload, in either direction.

end_reason.description: fin: both sides sent FIN. rst: a RST was seen. half_close: only one side sent FIN. capture_end: the capture ended while the session was open. new_connection: a SYN with a new initial sequence number replaced it. idle_timeout: UDP only, a later flow of the same 5-tuple follows after the idle timeout.

continues.description: Id of the earlier session of the same UDP 5-tuple that an idle split ended.

server_rtt_ms.description: Last SYN to the SYN ACK: the round trip between the capture point and the server.

client_rtt_ms.description: SYN ACK to the client ACK: the round trip between the capture point and the client.

rtt_ms.description: The sum of both, the end to end handshake time. Null unless the handshake is complete.

ip_bytes.description: Sum of the IP total lengths, headers included.

payload_bytes.description: Transport payload on the wire, counting every retransmitted copy.

stream_bytes.description: TCP only: distinct payload bytes captured, each counted once.

retransmitted_packets.description: TCP only: segments that repeat bytes seen before.

out_of_order_packets.description: TCP only: segments with new bytes that lie behind the highest byte seen, so they fill a hole.

missing_bytes.description: TCP only: bytes between the first and the highest offset that no segment carried.

turn.description: A run of consecutive deliveries in one direction. TCP deliveries are reassembled bytes in stream order. UDP deliveries are datagrams.

start_ns.description: When the first bytes of the turn were available, which is the time of the segment that closed the last hole before them.

packets.description: Deliveries merged into the turn. A hole fill can release several segments at once.

gap_before.description: TCP only: bytes that no segment carried, skipped before this turn. A turn with a gap always starts a new turn.

datagram_sizes.description: UDP only: payload size of each datagram.

data_b64.description: TCP, with --payloads: the bytes of the turn.

datagrams_b64.description: UDP, with --payloads: one entry per datagram.
